15 The vector diagram shows three coplanar forces acting on an object at P.
3 N
P
4 N
4 N
The magnitude of the resultant of these three forces is 1 N.
What is the direction of this resultant force?
A
B
C
D

hints: Notice the three arrows at P: $3\text{ N}$ straight up, $4\text{ N}$ straight right, and $4\text{ N}$ diagonally down-left at $45^{\circ}$ to the axes.
Resolve the diagonal $4\text{ N}$ force into south and west components using $4\cos 45^{\circ}$ and $4\sin 45^{\circ}$, then compare each with the opposite straight force.
Check the sign of the leftover $x$-force and the leftover $y$-force to decide whether the $1\text{ N}$ resultant points up or down and left or right.
walkthrough: Read components from the grid: take $+x$ east and $+y$ north, so the forces are $+3\text{ N}$ in $y$, $+4\text{ N}$ in $x$, and $4\text{ N}$ to the south-west at $45^{\circ}$.
Resolve the diagonal force: $F_x = -4\cos 45^{\circ}$ and $F_y = -4\sin 45^{\circ}$, each about $-2.8\text{ N}$.
Add $x$-components: $4 + (-2.8) \approx +1.2\text{ N}$, so there is a net force to the east.
Add $y$-components: $3 + (-2.8) \approx +0.2\text{ N}$, so there is a small net force to the north.
The combined vector therefore has magnitude about $1\text{ N}$ and points up and to the right, north-east. This is option D.

A.explanation: South-west is the direction of the $4\text{ N}$ diagonal force alone, not the sum of all three forces after the $3\text{ N}$ north and $4\text{ N}$ east are added.

B.explanation: South-east would need a net downward component, but the $3\text{ N}$ upward force largely balances the downward part of the diagonal $4\text{ N}$ force.

C.explanation: North-west would need a net leftward component, but the $4\text{ N}$ east force largely balances the leftward part of the diagonal $4\text{ N}$ force.

D.explanation: Both the east-west and north-south sums leave a small positive remainder to the east and north, giving a $1\text{ N}$ resultant to the north-east.
